title: Boolean algebras of formulas: equivalence, theories, and truth assignments
summary: Equivalent formulas form a Boolean algebra; closed theories become filters, and complete consistent theories are truth assignments.
abstract: Different formulas can make exactly the same demand on a truth assignment. For example, saying that two statements both hold has the same effect whichever is written first. We identify formulas that agree under every assignment and show that conjunction, disjunction, and negation then obey the laws of a Boolean algebra. A theory closed under consequence becomes a filter in this algebra: it contains the weaker consequences of its members and combines any two of them. The complete consistent theories are exactly the ultrafilters, and each of them is the collection of formulas true under one truth assignment. This connects the proof and truth viewpoints developed earlier with the algebra of union, intersection, and complement.
